contract: Open a seekable input, create the demuxer, read and fold every packet through confirmed end of file, collect stream and program metadata, and close the demuxer.
The native-index operation also reads every public index entry after packet delivery; an index trace is never substituted for an open-and-index benchmark.
Input loading, SHA-256 proof, process startup and output serialization are outside the measured operation. Rewind, parser and index allocation, packet production, folding and teardown are inside.
Supplement authored cases with 14 unmodified assets from the upstream MOV corpus. Each exercises open and public index through both input schedules. Fetch the original media by its pinned digest.
Ordinary windows are 65536 bytes with a work quantum of 4096; tiny windows are one byte with a quantum of three. Both use preloaded input and zero retained packets.
Every one of the 1020 declared traces is compared, including 48 explicit open refusals. Refusals are parity outcomes and are never timed as successful operations.
The 972 output labels cover 956 physical operations. Sixteen aliases retain separate parity checks and point explicitly to the same measured input, mode, arguments, policy and expected work.
The upstream cases also use a bounded compatibility view of complete edit rows, retaining the original count and any partial row in source metadata.
Candidate compatibility flags preserve bounded timing runs, bounded sync samples and terminal media declarations; three regular table cases use the standalone regular table recovery policy.
Successful ordered traces must be byte-identical and reproduce their expected packet, byte and digest counts. A work digest alone does not establish parity.
Expected work preserves the reference input SHA-256 and work-contract digest. Reference proof fields are checked separately from the candidate work projection.
